A local VPN is created on this device. All network traffic passes through it so the app can show which apps talk to whom. Nothing is ever sent to the makers of PrivacyGuard.
What does leave this phone:
â¢ Your DNS lookups, to the resolver you choose in Settings (Cloudflare 1.1.1.1 by default; encrypted to cloudflare-dns.com, dns.google or dns.quad9.net only when you turn on DoH).
â¢ Blocklist downloads, about once a week: raw.githubusercontent.com (StevenBlack, Hagezi), easylist.to and oisd.nl.
â¢ The Exodus tracker list, at most once a week: reports.exodus-privacy.eu.org.
â¢ Only if your organisation sets up SIEM shipping: inspected HTTPS requests and responses (app, host, time, headers and bodies, with personal data redacted when redaction is on) go to your organisationâs server.
Only if you turn them on in Settings:
â¢ Certificate Transparency checks: the domains you visit are sent to crt.sh.
â¢ The public IP check in Diagnostics: asks api.ipify.org.

Traffic logs are stored encrypted in the appâs private storage on this device. They leave the phone only when you share an export yourself (PCAP, CSV or IT report), or, if your organisation has set up SIEM shipping, as described above. You can delete them at any time from Settings.
